text_blocks.snippet: The 5-year relative survival rate for colon cancer is approximately 65%, meaning that 65% of people diagnosed with colon cancer are still alive 5 years later, after accounting for other potential causes of death. This overall survival rate varies significantly based on the stage of the cancer at diagnosis, with earlier detection leading to much higher survival rates.

list.title: Regional Cancer (spread to nearby lymph nodes):
list.snippet: If the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes, the 5-year survival rate is 72%.

list.title: Distant Cancer (spread to distant organs):
list.snippet: When the cancer has spread to distant parts of the body, the 5-year survival rate is 14%.
